questions.stem: What is the definition of a vertex in graph theory?

choices.B: A point representing an item or concept
choices.C: The weight or cost associated with an edge
choices.D: A cycle formed by a series of connected edges

questions.solution: In graph theory, a vertex (also known as a node) is a fundamental unit that represents an item or concept. Vertices serve as the building blocks for connecting different elements within a graph.
questions.explanation: Vertices are the basic units in a graph and denote entities or ideas connected by edges.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which describes an edge rather than a vertex.

questions.stem: What is the term for the lines connecting vertices in a graph?
questions.solution: In graph theory, edges are the connections that link vertices together within a graph.
questions.explanation: Edges define the relationships between vertices and enable traversal or flow within the graph structure.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which refers to the points rather than the connections.

choices.A: Vertices are connected by undirected edges
choices.B: Edges have no direction and can be traversed in either direction
choices.C: Edges have a fixed starting and ending vertex
choices.D: Vertices cannot repeat within an edge

questions.solution: A directed graph is a type of graph where edges possess a specific direction, indicating a one-way relationship between vertices.
questions.explanation: In directed graphs, edges have an arrow-like orientation, allowing traversal or flow from the starting vertex to the ending vertex only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which describes an undirected graph.

questions.stem: What property differentiates an undirected graph from a directed graph?

choices.A: Vertices are connected by undirected edges
choices.B: Edges have no direction and can be traversed in either direction
choices.C: Edges have a fixed starting and ending vertex
choices.D: Vertices cannot repeat within an edge

questions.solution: An undirected graph has edges that connect vertices symmetrically, allowing traversal or flow in both directions, unlike directed graphs.
questions.explanation: In contrast to directed graphs, undirected graphs do not have a fixed starting and ending vertex; their edges connect nodes equally in either direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing C, which describes a directed graph.

questions.stem: What is the term for an edge that connects a vertex to itself?
questions.solution: In graph theory, a loop is an edge that connects a vertex to itself, forming a cycle within the vertex.
questions.explanation: Loops are self-referential connections and can be found in both directed and undirected graphs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which refers to a basic connection between two different vertices.

questions.stem: What value is typically assigned to edges in an unweighted graph?
questions.solution: An unweighted graph assigns a value of one (or no explicit value) to its edges, indicating equal cost or distance between connected vertices.
questions.explanation: Unweighted graphs emphasize connectivity rather than numerical relationships between vertices; the assigned edge value is often symbolic.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which may be used in certain contexts but is not standard for unweighted graphs.

questions.stem: What is a tree in graph theory?

choices.A: A cycle-free graph with the minimum number of edges
choices.B: A connected graph with no cycles and an equal number of vertices and edges
choices.C: A complete graph where every vertex is connected to every other vertex
choices.D: A disconnected graph with a single path between any two vertices

questions.solution: In graph theory, a tree is a connected graph that contains no cycles and has exactly one path between any two vertices.
questions.explanation: Trees are acyclic graphs characterized by their unique route between any pair of nodes.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, which describes a forest rather than a tree.
